# Appendix A {#sec-appenda}

This appendix contains information on the small mammal datasets used to construct many of the data analysis examples. The original datasets were downloaded from the [National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON)](https://www.neonscience.org/). Once downloaded, the data were filtered to exclude incomplete or possibly incorrect records, and to update taxonomy to 2026 conventions. The data were then reorganized into 4 tables:

1. **neon-grids.csv**: contains metadata on trapping grids.
1. **neon-captures.csv**: contains small mammal capture data.
1. **neon-measures.csv**: contains small mammal body mass and standard measurements.
1. **neon-taxa.csv**: contains taxonomic definitions for each species in the capture data.

## Data dictionary

### `neon-grids.csv`

- **domain**: sampling region or *domain* as defined by NEON.
- **site**: unique four letter code for site name.
- **grid**: unique grid ID, nested within site.
- **lat**: latitude in degrees north.
- **lon**: longitude in degrees east.
- **elev**: elevation in m.
- **nlcd**: dominant NLCD land cover type within grid.

### `neon-captures.csv`

- **grid**: unique grid ID (corresponds to `neon-grids$grid`
- **AMHA** through **ZATR**: number of captures of each small mammal species. Four-letter species abbreviations correspond to neon-taxa.csv, column `abb`.

### `neon-measures.csv`

### `neon-taxa.csv`


## Packages

The following packages were used:

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(ritis)
library(missForest)
```

## Data download

The first step was to download all small mammal data from June 2013 through December 2023. The data used were finalized, non-provisional data. The data were downloaded and unzipped to a folder, `top.dir`. 

```{r}
#| eval: false

## Unzipped the resulting download into 
top.dir <- "K:/_neon/NEON_count-small-mammals"
```

The data at this point were organized by folders, with each folder containing the data from a single site and trapping bout. 

## Read data into memory

```{r}
#| eval: false


# get folder names
folds <- dir(top.dir)

# only need the folders, which have "RELEASE-20" 
# in their names
folds <- folds[grep("RELEASE-20", folds)]
n.folds <- length(folds)

# which columns do we want from basic dataset?
use.cols1 <- c("domainID", "siteID", "plotID",
              "decimalLatitude",
              "decimalLongitude", "elevation",
              "nlcdClass", "tagID",
              "scientificName", "sex", "lifeStage",
              "pregnancyStatus", "hindfootLength",
              "earLength",
              "tailLength", "totalLength", "weight",
              "tickNumber")  

# mlist for measured specimens
# spplist for species at each location
#   (includes extra species not in basic dataset)
spplist <- mlist <- vector("list", length=n.folds)
i <- 1

for(i in 1:n.folds){
  ifold <- paste(top.dir, folds[i], sep="/")
  ifile <- dir(ifold)
  
  # basic file--has individual captures
  ifile <- ifile[grep("_pertrapnight", ifile)]
  ix <- read.csv(paste(ifold, ifile, sep="/"))
  
  # only need captures
  ix <- ix[which(ix$trapStatus == "5 - capture"),]
  ispp <- character(0)
  
  # get basic captures, if any
  if(nrow(ix) > 0){
    ix <- ix[,use.cols1]
    mlist[[i]] <- ix
    # vector of species
    ispp <- sort(unique(ix$scientificName))
  }

  # get vouchers, if any
  # voucher file doesn't have any measurement data,
  # so just inspect to get unique species
  vfile <- dir(ifold)
  vfile <- vfile[grep("_voucher", vfile)]
  if(length(vfile) > 0){
    vx <- read.csv(paste(ifold, vfile, sep="/"))
    if(nrow(vx) > 0){
      # unique species in vouchers ## will have to remove nonmammals
      vspp <- sort(unique(vx$scientificName))  
      if(length(vspp) > 0){
        # combine with species in basic data
        ispp <- sort(union(ispp, vspp))  
      }#if any vspp
    }# if any rows in vx
    rm(vx)
  }#if vfile exists

  # save species to species list
  spplist[[i]] <- ispp
 
  rm(ix)
  rm(ispp)
  
  cat("folder", i, "of", n.folds, "done!\n")
  flush.console()
}

# compile measurement data
res <- do.call(rbind, mlist)
```

## Update taxonomy

```{r}
#| eval: false

# need to rectify taxonomy before interpolating measurements, 
# so we use the right animals for each interpolation
tax <- data.frame(dbin=sort(unique(res$scientificName)))
tax$dgen <- sapply(strsplit(tax$dbin, " "), "[", 1)
tax$dspp <- sapply(strsplit(tax$dbin, " "), "[", 2)
tax$tsn <- NA
tax$valid <- NA
for(i in 1:nrow(tax)){
  ires <- search_scientific(tax$dbin[i])
  if(nrow(ires) == 0) next
  flag <- which(ires$combinedName == tax$dbin[i])
  itsn <- ires$tsn[flag]
  tax$tsn[i] <- itsn
  valid <- as.data.frame(usage(itsn))$taxonUsageRating[1]
  tax$valid[i] <- valid
  cat("taxon", i, "of", nrow(tax), "complete!\n")
  flush.console()
}

tax$tsn[1] <- "180298"
tax$valid[1] <- "valid"

# igen is correct genus to use when interpolating
tax$igen <- tax$dgen

tax$igen[1] <- "Microtus"

tax[which(tax$valid == "invalid"),]

flag <- which(tax$dbin == "Blarina brevicauda")
```

## clean up individual IDs

```{r}
#| eval: false

# how certain are we that each individual was identified consistently?
aa <- rev(sort(table(res$tagID)))
res[which(res$tagID == "NEON.MAM.D15.L2927"),]
rm(aa)

## how many species are associated with each tag?
utags <- sort(unique(res$tagID))
ntags <- length(utags)
ind.ag <- aggregate(scientificName~tagID, data=res,
                    function(x){length(unique(x))})
head(ind.ag)
# almost all (96.8%) are associated with only 1 species
# 3.2% have 2 species; 0.05% have 3 species
table(ind.ag$scientificName)
#    1     2     3 
#60466  1983    34 
table(ind.ag$scientificName)/ntags

# any way to resolve?
spp2 <- ind.ag$tagID[which(ind.ag$scientificName == 2)]

# what kinds of issues are there?
df2 <- aggregate(scientificName~tagID, data=res[which(res$tagID %in% spp2),],
                 function(x){paste(sort(unique(x)), collapse="__")})
rev(sort(table(df2$scientificName)))

#### conclusion: only keep individuals with consistent identity
#### doesn't guarantee correct, just consistent
spp1 <- ind.ag$tagID[which(ind.ag$scientificName == 1)]
nrow(res)
res <- res[which(res$tagID %in% spp1),]
nrow(res)                                                 

summary(res)

### species in dataset

tax$abb <- toupper(tax$abb)
```

## organize grid metadata

```{r}
#| eval: false

#### make a table of grids (plots)
ugrids <- sort(unique(res$plotID))
ngrids <- length(ugrids)
grd <- data.frame(grid=ugrids)
grd$site <- sapply(strsplit(grd$grid, "_"), "[", 1)
matchx <- match(grd$grid, res$plotID)
grd$domain <- res$domainID[matchx]
grd$lat <- res$decimalLatitude[matchx]
grd$lon <- res$decimalLongitude[matchx]
grd$elev <- res$elevation[matchx]
grd$nlcd <- res$nlcdClass[matchx]
grd <- grd[,c(3, 2, 1, 4:7)]

doms <- c("Northeast", "Midatlantic", "Southeast", "Atlantic Neotropical",
          "Great Lakes", "Prairie Peninsula", "Appalachians", "Ozarks",
          "Northern Plains", "Central Plains", "Southern Plains", 
          "Northern Rockies", "Southern Rockies", "Desert Southwest",
          "Great Basin", "Pacific Northwest", "Pacific Southwest")
doms <- paste0("D", formatC(1:19, width=2, flag="0"), "_", doms)

names(doms) <- sapply(strsplit(doms, "_"), "[", 1)
grd$domain <- doms[grd$domain]

### export version of grids
grd <- grd[order(grd$domain, grd$grid),]

```


## Clean up individual measurement data

```{r}
#| eval: false

### finalize measurements
met1 <- res[,c("plotID", "tagID", "abb", "sex", "hindfootLength", "earLength",
              "tailLength", "totalLength", "weight", "tickNumber")]
mag1 <- aggregate(weight~tagID, data=met1, mean, na.rm=TRUE)
mag2 <- aggregate(totalLength~tagID, data=met1, mean, na.rm=TRUE)
mag3 <- aggregate(tailLength~tagID, data=met1, mean, na.rm=TRUE)
mag4 <- aggregate(hindfootLength~tagID, data=met1, mean, na.rm=TRUE)
mag5 <- aggregate(earLength~tagID, data=met1, mean, na.rm=TRUE)

# combine nonmissing values
met <- data.frame(tag=sort(unique(met1$tagID)))
met$mass   <- mag1$weight[match(met$tag, mag1$tagID)]
met$totlen <- mag2$totalLength[match(met$tag, mag2$tagID)]
met$tail   <- mag3$tailLength[match(met$tag, mag3$tagID)]
met$foot   <- mag4$hindfootLength[match(met$tag, mag4$tagID)]
met$pinna  <- mag5$earLength[match(met$tag, mag5$tagID)]

# get individuals with all measurements
met$spp <- met1$abb[match(met$tag, met1$tagID)]
met.all <- met[complete.cases(met),]
nrow(met.all)

# what about those missing only 1 measurement?
met$nonmiss <- apply(met[,c(2:6)], 1, function(x){length(which(!is.na(x)))})
table(met$nonmiss)

met4 <- met[which(met$nonmiss >= 4),]
met4$miss <- as.numeric(apply(met4[,2:6], 1, function(x){which(is.na(x))}))
met4$miss <- names(met4)[met4$miss+1]
ftable(miss~spp, data=met4)

# interpolate missing measurements
met4$genus <- tax$dgen[match(met4$spp, tax$abb)]
# combine a few genera to get more robust interpolations
met4$genus[which(met4$genus == "Alexandromys")] <- "Microtus"
met4$genus[which(met4$genus == "Ictidomys")] <- "Spermophilus"
met4$genus[which(met4$genus == "Lemmiscus")] <- "Lemmus"
met4$genus[which(met4$genus == "Synaptomys")] <- "Lemmus"
met4$genus[which(met4$genus == "Dicrostonyx")] <- "Lemmus"
met4$genus[which(met4$genus == "Phenacomys")] <- "Microtus"
table(met4$genus)


# install.packages("missForest")
library(missForest)

ugenera <- sort(unique(met4$genus))
ngenera <- length(ugenera)
for(i in 1:ngenera){
  cat("starting genus", ugenera[i], "!\n")
  flush.console()
  flag <- which(met4$genus == ugenera[i])
  ix <- met4[flag, 2:6]
  imput <- missForest(ix)
  met4[flag,2:6] <- round(imput$ximp,0)
  cat("genus", i, "of", ngenera, "imputed!\n")
  flush.console()
}

# remove unneeded variables
met4$miss <- NULL
met4$genus <- NULL
met4$nonmiss <- NULL

# add back in other variables
met4$sex <- met1$sex[match(met4$tag, met1$tagID)]
met4$plot <- met1$plotID[match(met4$tag, met1$tagID)]

# rearrange
met4 <- met4[,c(9, 1, 8, 7, 2:6)]
names(met4)[1] <- "grid"
##### met4 is the output ready measurement dataset

## checks: must be TRUE:
all(met4$grid %in% grd$grid)
all(met4$spp %in% tax$abb)
```

## finalize taxonomy

```{r}
#| eval: false

# finalize tax
tax$X <- NULL
xtax <- tax[,c(7, 5, 4, 1)]
xtax$order <- NA
xtax$suborder <- NA
xtax$superfamily <- NA
xtax$family <- NA
xtax$subfamily <- NA
xtax$genus <- NA
xtax$species <- NA

ntax <- nrow(xtax)
for(i in 1:ntax){
  itsn <- xtax$tsn[i]
  ih <- as.data.frame(hierarchy_full(itsn))
  xtax$order[i] <- ih$taxonname[which(ih$rankname == "Order")]
  if("Suborder" %in% ih$rankname){
    xtax$suborder[i] <- ih$taxonname[which(ih$rankname == "Suborder")]
  }
  if("Superfamily" %in% ih$rankname){
    xtax$superfamily[i] <- ih$taxonname[which(ih$rankname == "Superfamily")]
  }
  xtax$family[i] <- ih$taxonname[which(ih$rankname == "Family")]
  if("Subfamily" %in% ih$rankname){
    xtax$subfamily[i] <- ih$taxonname[which(ih$rankname == "Subfamily")]
  }
  xtax$genus[i] <- ih$taxonname[which(ih$rankname == "Genus")]
  xtax$species[i] <- ih$taxonname[which(ih$rankname == "Species")]
  cat("taxon", i, "of", ntax, "complete!\n")
  flush.console()
}

head(xtax)
xtax$dbin <- NULL
xtax <- xtax[order(xtax$abb),]
xtax$valid <- NULL
xtax <- xtax[,c(1, 2, 9, 3:8)]
rownames(xtax) <- NULL
all(table(xtax$spp) == 1)
xtax <- xtax[-which(xtax$tsn == 931114),]
xtax <- xtax[-which(xtax$tsn == 180349)[1],]
all(table(xtax$spp) == 1)
rownames(xtax) <- NULL

#### xtax is export ready version of taxonomy
```

## Capture numbers

```{r}
#| eval: false

## species presence matrix is grid x species matrix
ugrid <- sort(unique(grd$grid))
ngrid <- length(ugrid)

ntax <- nrow(xtax)
pmat <- matrix(0, nrow=ngrid, ncol=ntax)
colnames(pmat) <- sort(xtax$abb)
rownames(pmat) <- ugrid

all(res$abb %in% colnames(pmat))

i <- 1
for(i in 1:ngrid){
  flag <- which(res$plotID == ugrid[i])
  ispp <- table(res$abb[flag])
  pmat[i,names(ispp)] <- ispp
  cat("grid", i, "of", ngrid, "complete!\n")
  flush.console()
}

pmat <- as.data.frame(pmat)
pmat <- cbind(data.frame(grid=rownames(pmat)), pmat)
rownames(pmat) <- NULL


```

```{r}
out.name <- "neon-grids.csv"
out.path <- paste(data.dir, out.name, sep="/")
write.csv(out, out.path, row.names=FALSE)

# taxa

out.name <- "neon-taxa.csv"
out.path <- paste(data.dir, out.name, sep="/")
```
